questions.question: What is the fundamental structural rule for a word to be classified as ghayr munsarif?
options: Three asbāb simultaneously present, or two asbāb each qā'im maqām as-sababayn
Two asbāb simultaneously present, or one sabab that is qā'im maqām as-sababayn
One sabab alone is always sufficient for ghayr munsarif status
Two asbāb simultaneously present, with at least one being alamiyyah
questions.explanation: A word is ghayr munsarif when either two asbāb are simultaneously present, or one sabab is present that is qā'im maqām as-sababayn — so weighty it stands in place of two reasons on its own.

questions.question: Which sign of ta'nīth does NOT act as qā'im maqām as-sababayn?
options: Both Alif Maqsūra and Alif Mamdūda
Alif Maqsūra (ى)
Alif Mamdūda (اء)
Tā' Marbūtah (ة)
questions.explanation: Tā' Marbūtah counts as only one sabab — it requires a second sabab alongside it to produce ghayr munsarif status. Alif Maqsūra and Alif Mamdūda each stand alone as qā'im maqām as-sababayn.

questions.question: Why is شَيْطَان munsarif while إِبْلِيس is ghayr munsarif?
options: شَيْطَان follows a pattern of jama' muntaha al-jumūm while إِبْلِيس does not
شَيْطَان carries tā' marbūtah providing tā'nīth while إِبْلِيس does not
شَيْطَان is a common noun with no alamiyyah while إِبْلِيس has both alamiyyah and ʿujmah
شَيْطَان is Arabic in origin while إِبْلِيس is non-Arabic, so only إِبْلِيس has ʿujmah
questions.explanation: شَيْطَان is a common noun applicable to any evil jinn — it has no alamiyyah, so ʿujmah alone gives only one sabab → munsarif. إِبْلِيس is a proper name (alamiyyah) of non-Arabic origin (ʿujmah) — two asbāb → ghayr munsarif.

questions.question: A non-Arabic proper name has three root letters with a sukūn on the middle letter. What is its ruling regarding ghayr munsarif?
options: Ghayr munsarif, because alamiyyah and ʿujmah together always produce ghayr munsarif
Munsarif, because its brevity (sulāsī with sākin middle) offsets the ʿujmah condition
Ghayr munsarif, because ʿujmah alone is sufficient for any proper noun
Munsarif, because non-Arabic names with fewer than four letters are exempt from ʿujmah
questions.explanation: A sulāsī non-Arabic proper noun with a sākin middle letter is too 'light' — its brevity offsets the ʿujmah condition. This is why نُوح and لُوط are munsarif despite being non-Arabic Prophets' names.

questions.question: Which two patterns constitute جَمْعُ مُنْتَهَى الْجُمُوع?
options: فَعَائِل and مَفَاعِيل
مَفَاعِل and فَعَالِل
فَعَالِل and فَعَالِيل
مَفَاعِل and مَفَاعِيل
questions.explanation: The two patterns are مَفَاعِل (e.g., مَسَاجِد) and مَفَاعِيل (e.g., مَصَابِيح). Both act as qā'im maqām as-sababayn.

questions.question: Which example fails the tarkīb sabab for ghayr munsarif because of iḍāfah?
options: إِبْلِيس
عَبْدُ اللَّهِ
بَعْلَبَكَّ
حَمْرَاء
questions.explanation: عَبْدُ اللَّهِ has an iḍāfah relationship — عَبْد is muḍāf and اللَّه is muḍāf ilayhi — which disqualifies it from the tarkīb sabab, making it munsarif.

questions.question: What two grammatical effects distinguish a غَيْرُ مُنْصَرِف noun from a munsarif noun?
options: It does not accept ال and takes fatḥah in every iʿrāb state
It does not accept ال and takes ḍammah instead of fatḥah in the marfūʿ state
It does not accept tanwīn and takes fatḥah instead of kasrah in the majrūr state
It does not accept tanwīn and takes kasrah instead of fatḥah in the majrūr state
questions.explanation: A ghayr munsarif noun (diptote) does not accept tanwīn, and in the majrūr state it takes fatḥah rather than the usual kasrah.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three asbāb that are قَائِمٌ مَقَامَ السَّبَبَيْن?
options: Alif Maqsūra
Jama' Muntaha al-Jumūm
Tā' Marbūtah
Alif Mamdūda
questions.explanation: The three asbāb that carry the weight of two are: Alif Maqsūra, Alif Mamdūda, and Jama' Muntaha al-Jumūm. Tā' Marbūtah counts as only one sabab and is not in this group.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between عَلَمِيَّة and maʿrifah?
options: Every maʿrifah is an alam, but not every alam is a maʿrifah
Every alam is a maʿrifah, but not every maʿrifah is an alam
Neither every maʿrifah is an alam, nor every alam is a maʿrifah
Every maʿrifah is an alam, and every alam is a maʿrifah
questions.explanation: The relationship is one-directional: every alam is necessarily maʿrifah, but a maʿrifah (like الرَّجُلُ) may refer to an unspecified individual and thus is not an alam.

questions.question: What additional sabab must accompany عُجْمَة for a word to be ghayr munsarif?
options: Jama' Muntaha al-Jumūm
Alamiyyah
Tarkīb
Tā' Marbūtah
questions.explanation: ʿUjmah alone provides only one sabab. It must be paired with alamiyyah — the word must also be a proper noun in its original language — to produce ghayr munsarif status.

questions.question: Why is جَمْعُ مُنْتَهَى الْجُمُوع called 'terminal' (muntahā)?
options: Because no further plural can be formed from it
Because it contains the maximum number of syllables allowed in Arabic
Because it always ends in an alif followed by two consonants
Because it always appears at the end of a sentence
questions.explanation: It is 'terminal' because no further plural can be formed from it — it is the final stage of pluralization beyond which the word cannot be pluralized again.

questions.question: Which word has its femininity marked by an أَلِف مَقْصُورَة?
options: فَاطِمَة
حَمْرَاء
مَسَاجِد
حُبْلَى
questions.explanation: Alif Maqsūra is written as ى at the end of a word; حُبْلَى is an example of a word whose femininity is marked by this alif.

questions.question: Which word has its femininity marked by an أَلِف مَمْدُودَة?
options: حُبْلَى
مَصَابِيح
دَوَابّ
حَمْرَاء
questions.explanation: Alif Mamdūda is an alif followed by hamzah at the end of a word; حَمْرَاء is an example where this alif marks femininity.

questions.question: Which two grammatical relationships disqualify a compound from the تَرْكِيب sabab?
options: Isnād and tā'nīth
ʿUjmah and alamiyyah
Iḍāfah and isnād
Jama' muntaha al-jumūm and tā' marbūtah
questions.explanation: If iḍāfah (possessive/genitive construction) or isnād (predicate-subject relation) exists between the two parts of a compound, it is disqualified from the tarkīb sabab.

questions.question: Why is عَبْدُ اللَّهِ munsarif despite being a compound proper noun?
options: Because عَبْد is a common noun rather than a proper noun
Because it has an isnād relationship between its two parts
Because it contains the name of Allah, which overrides the tarkīb rule
Because it has an iḍāfah relationship between its two parts
questions.explanation: عَبْدُ اللَّهِ has an iḍāfah relationship — عَبْد is muḍāf and اللَّه is muḍāf ilayhi — which disqualifies it from the tarkīb sabab, making it munsarif.

questions.question: In the context of جَمْعُ مُنْتَهَى الْجُمُوع, when is a مُشَدَّد letter legally significant?
options: When only one letter follows the alif of the plural
When the word is a non-Arabic proper noun
When three letters follow the alif of the plural
When two letters follow the alif of the plural, with the first being sākin
questions.explanation: Shadda becomes legally significant in jama' muntaha al-jumūm when only one letter follows the alif — that single letter must be mushaddad for the pattern to be valid, as in دَوَابّ.

questions.question: According to this passage, what two descriptors define الْفَاسِقِينَ?
options: Ahl al-Kitāb who specifically reject Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
Those who break covenants and sever ties of kinship
Those who go outside Allah's obedience and deny His signs
Those who spread fitnah and commit shirk openly
questions.explanation: The Fasiqeen are those who have stepped outside Allah's obedience (al-khārijīn ʿan ṭāʿat Allāh) and those who deny and reject Allah's signs (al-jāḥidīn bi-āyātihi).

questions.question: Why is نَقْضُ الْعَهْدِ (breaking of covenants) specific to Ahl al-Kitāb and not to the Mushrikeen?
options: The Mushrikeen received a different type of mīthāq not addressed in this passage
The Mushrikeen had no divine book containing formal covenants to break
The Mushrikeen were excused because no messenger had been sent to them
The Mushrikeen broke their covenants before the Qurʾān was revealed
questions.explanation: The Mushrikeen never received a divine book containing such formal covenants — they had no mīthāq of this kind to break, which is why this characteristic is specific to Ahl al-Kitāb.

questions.question: Of the three 'severed connections' described in this passage, which one is specific to Ahl al-Kitāb?
options: Rejecting some prophets while accepting others
Abandoning loyalty bonds with believers
Spreading kufr and shirk
Severing ties of kinship (qat' al-arḥām)
questions.explanation: Rejecting some prophets while accepting others — e.g., accepting Mūsā but rejecting Muḥammad ﷺ — is specific to Ahl al-Kitāb. Severing kinship ties and abandoning loyalty bonds with believers apply generally.

questions.question: What is identified as the worst form of إِفْسَادٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ in this passage?
options: Spreading kufr and shirk
Preventing people from accepting Islam
Raising doubts about the Qurʾān
Severing ties of kinship
questions.explanation: The worst form of ifsād is spreading kufr and shirk. The supporting Qurʾānic phrase is 'الْفِتْنَةُ أَشَدُّ مِنَ الْقَتْلِ' from Surah Al-Baqarah itself.

questions.question: What type of rhetorical device is كَيْفَ in Ayah 28?
options: An interrogative of rebuke and denial (inkār) scolding the disbelievers
A rhetorical question expecting a positive affirmation
A conditional particle introducing the five stages of existence
A genuine request for information addressed to the disbelievers
questions.explanation: Kayfa here is an interrogative of rebuke and denial (inkār) — it scolds and rejects the disbelievers' stance; it is not a genuine request for information.

questions.question: What is the logical proof for the ease of resurrection derived from Ayah 29?
options: Allah created man once from clay, so He can certainly recreate him from it
The seven heavens contain enough capacity to house all resurrected souls
If Allah accomplished the incomparably greater act of creating the entire universe, resurrection of a single human is even more easily within His power
The framework of creation was designed with resurrection as its ultimate purpose
questions.explanation: Allah created the entire universe — earth, seven heavens, all planets and galaxies — an act of far greater magnitude than resurrecting one human. If He accomplished the greater, the lesser (resurrection) is even more easily within His power.

questions.question: The root meaning of fisq is 'going outside.' What specifically are الْفَاسِقِينَ going outside of?
options: The boundaries of the masjid
The obedience of Allah
The covenant of the Prophets
The community of believers
questions.explanation: The Fasiqeen are those going outside the obedience of Allah (ṭāʿat Allāh) — this is the specific meaning the passage establishes.

questions.question: What distinguishes a مِيثَاق from a general عَهْد?
options: A mīthāq is an affirmed, witnessed, and binding covenant backed by proofs and evidences
A mīthāq is a covenant with Allah while an ʿahd is a covenant between people
A mīthāq is an informal verbal agreement while an ʿahd is a written contract
A mīthāq applies only to Ahl al-Kitāb while an ʿahd applies universally
questions.explanation: A mīthāq is an affirmed, witnessed, and binding covenant backed by proofs and evidences — making its violation far more grave than breaking an ordinary agreement (ʿahd).

questions.question: What does Allah command regarding قَطْعُ الأَرْحَام (family ties)?
options: That they be redefined to include only close relatives
That they be maintained and upheld
That they be severed if they lead to fitnah
That they be renewed through formal covenants
questions.explanation: Allah commands that family ties (arḥām) be maintained and upheld. Severing these ties is listed here as a defining characteristic of the Fasiqeen.

questions.question: In the context of إِفْسَادٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ in this passage, what does فِتْنَة specifically mean?
options: Discord and conflict within the Muslim community
Temptation toward worldly desires
The spreading of kufr and shirk
Trials and hardships sent by Allah as a test
questions.explanation: In this passage, fitnah specifically means the spreading of kufr and shirk — not temptation generally, but active propagation of disbelief and polytheism.

questions.question: From which surah is الْفِتْنَةُ أَشَدُّ مِنَ الْقَتْلِ taken?
options: Surah Al-Anfāl
Surah An-Nisāʾ
Surah Al-Baqarah
Surah Āl ʿImrān
questions.explanation: This phrase is from Surah Al-Baqarah. All mufassirūn agree that fitnah here means the spreading of kufr and shirk.

questions.question: بَعْث is one of the five stages of human existence in Ayah 28. Which stage is it?
options: Death at the appointed time (stage three)
Return to Allah for reckoning (stage five)
Life in this world (stage two)
Resurrection from the graves (stage four)
questions.explanation: Baʿth is stage four: resurrection — Allah reviving the dead from their graves (baʿth min al-qubūr).

questions.question: How must اسْتَوَى be understood when applied to Allah in Ayah 29?
options: Literally and without any interpretation
As a metaphor for His omniscience over the heavens
As referring to the physical arrangement of the seven heavens
As it befits Allah's majesty, without likening it to the rising of a created being
questions.explanation: Istawā must be understood as it befits Allah's majesty — without likening it to the rising of a created being or making any anthropomorphic comparison.

questions.question: Both أَمَاتَ and أَحْيَا are Form IV (bāb ifʿāl). What grammatical feature of Form IV do their meanings reflect?
options: Reflexivity — the subject acts upon itself
Passivity — the subject receives the action
Intensification — a more intense form of the base action
Causativity — causing something to happen to another
questions.explanation: Form IV conveys causativity: amāta means 'to cause to die' and aḥyā means 'to cause to live / to give life' — the subject causes the action to occur in another.

questions.question: What is the دَلِيلُ الْقُدْرَةِ الْبَاهِرَةِ referred to in Ayah 29?
options: The creation of the earth and seven heavens
The resurrection of the dead on the Day of Judgment
The revelation of the Qurʾān to the Prophet ﷺ
The creation of the first human being from clay
questions.explanation: The dalīl is the creation of the earth and seven heavens. It proves Allah's overwhelming, absolute power — and by extension, that resurrection is entirely within His ability.

questions.question: Why did the teacher decline to cover بَلَاغَة in these āyāt?
options: The mufassirūn discourage discussing balāghah in passages about the Fasiqeen
The balāghah of these verses is too advanced even for the teacher to explain
Balāghah analysis is not part of the tafseer curriculum at any level
The students have not yet studied a balāghah textbook, so teaching it would consume too much time and divert from the required curriculum
questions.explanation: The teacher declined because the students have not yet studied a balāghah textbook; introducing it now would consume too much time and divert from the required tafseer curriculum.

questions.question: Why is qaḍāʾ waived for missed ṣalāh during ḥayḍ but required for missed fasts?
options: Fasting can be made up one day at a time while multiple ṣalawāt in a day cannot
There is no Qurʾānic evidence requiring the makeup of ṣalāh missed during ḥayḍ
Ṣalāh is more obligatory than fasting, so its makeup would be more burdensome
Missing approximately 600 ṣalawāt per year constitutes ḥaraj, while making up 10 fasting days spread over 11 months does not
questions.explanation: The principle is ḥaraj — recognized hardship Sharīʿah relieves through concession. A woman may miss ~600 ṣalawāt per year (ḥaraj → qaḍāʾ waived), but misses at most 10 fasting days per month; making up one per month closes the gap, so no ḥaraj and qaḍāʾ is required.

questions.question: What criterion determines whether a space is a masjid (where a ḥāʾiḍah may not enter the prayer hall) rather than a muṣallā?
options: Whether the space has a permanently appointed imam
Formal legal designation as waqf exclusively for the purpose of a masjid
The presence of a permanent dome and minaret
Whether the space hosts Jumuʿah prayers
questions.explanation: The determining criterion is intention and formal legal designation (waqf) — not architectural features. A dome and minaret are historical symbols, not juridical markers; the Tāj Maḥal has both yet is not a masjid.

questions.question: Under what timing conditions is vaginal bleeding classified as اسْتِحَاضَة rather than ḥayḍ?
options: When it is lighter in color or flow than her normal ḥayḍ
When it lasts less than 3 days or more than 10 days
When it occurs outside the woman's established habit dates
When it lasts between 3 and 10 days
questions.explanation: Istiḥāḍah is vaginal bleeding that is less than 3 days (below the minimum for ḥayḍ) or more than 10 days (above the maximum for ḥayḍ) in duration.

questions.question: A woman with an established ʿādah of 7 days bleeds for 11 days. How are days 8 through 10 classified?
options: A new ḥayḍ cycle beginning on day 8
Ṭuhr, because the established habit period has already ended
Ḥayḍ, because they are still within the 10-day maximum
Istiḥāḍah, because they exceed her established habit of 7 days
questions.explanation: Days 8–10 are still classified as ḥayḍ because they fall within the 10-day maximum. She performs ghusl on day 10 when ḥayḍ ends at the cap; days 11 onward are istiḥāḍah.

questions.question: What makes a ṭalāq bidʿī (an impermissible innovation in divorce)?
options: Pronouncing three ṭalāqs simultaneously, or pronouncing any ṭalāq during ḥayḍ
Pronouncing ṭalāq before the couple has been married for one full year
Pronouncing three ṭalāqs across three separate periods of ṭuhr
Pronouncing one ṭalāq during a single period of ṭuhr without witnesses
questions.explanation: Ṭalāq bidʿī includes pronouncing three ṭalāqs simultaneously, or giving any ṭalāq while the wife is in ḥayḍ — both are impermissible.

questions.question: Under Imām al-Shāfiʿī's position, what must a maʿdhūr woman do to pray nāfil ṣalāh after her farḍ?
options: Perform a complete ghusl before each nāfil ṣalāh
Use the same wuḍūʾ until the current ṣalāh time exits
Use the same wuḍūʾ until the next ṣalāh time begins
Make a fresh wuḍūʾ before each nāfil ṣalāh
questions.explanation: Under Imām al-Shāfiʿī's position, wuḍūʾ is valid only for that single farḍ ṣalāh — nāfil after it requires a new wuḍūʾ. Under the Ḥanafī position (Abū Ḥanīfah/Abū Yūsuf), the same wuḍūʾ lasts until the next ṣalāh time begins.

questions.question: What established analogy (ḥukm) does اسْتِحَاضَة share?
options: The ḥukm of minor ritual impurity requiring only wuḍūʾ
The ḥukm of major ritual impurity (janābah)
The ḥukm of a nosebleed (ḥukm al-ruʿāf)
The ḥukm of ḥayḍ with reduced restrictions
questions.explanation: Istiḥāḍah shares the ḥukm of a nosebleed (ḥukm al-ruʿāf): it is a minor impurity that does not prevent ṣalāh, fasting, or conjugal relations — worship continues normally.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a مَعْذُور in the Ḥanafī school?
options: A person too ill to stand during ṣalāh
A person who forgets to renew wuḍūʾ before ṣalāh
A traveler who cannot find water for wuḍūʾ
A person with chronic urinary incontinence
questions.explanation: A maʿdhūr has a continuous excuse that invalidates wuḍūʾ; examples include a woman with continuous istiḥāḍah, a person with chronic urinary incontinence, and a person with a continuously bleeding wound.

questions.question: If a مُبْتَدَأَة's very first cycle lasts 12 days, what becomes her established ʿādah?
options: 3 days, the minimum for ḥayḍ
7 days, the average for most women
12 days, matching the full duration of her first cycle
10 days, the legal maximum
questions.explanation: Days 1–10 are ḥayḍ (the legal maximum); days 11–12 are istiḥāḍah. Her ʿādah becomes 10 days — the maximum her first cycle produced within the legal limit.

questions.question: If a مُعْتَادَة whose ʿādah is 8 days bleeds for 9 days (still within the 10-day max), what is the ruling?
options: Day 9 triggers a new ḥayḍ cycle and her ʿādah resets to 1 day
She must consult a scholar before any classification can be made
All 9 days are ḥayḍ and her ʿādah changes to 9 days
Only the first 8 days are ḥayḍ; day 9 is istiḥāḍah; ʿādah does not change
questions.explanation: All 9 days are classified as ḥayḍ since they fall within the 10-day maximum. Her ʿādah changes — 9 days becomes her updated established habit.

questions.question: Why can a general ruling not be applied directly to a مُسْتَرِيبَة?
options: She has no established ʿādah and requires individualized guidance from a qualified scholar
She must wait three full cycles before any classification can be made
Her condition is too rare to have an established ruling in classical fiqh
The Ḥanafī school has not issued a position on her specific condition
questions.explanation: A mustaribah's situation is a 'moving target' — she has no established habit, so a general ruling cannot apply. She needs individualized guidance from a qualified muftī/ʿālim who can issue a fatwā specific to her condition.

questions.question: What is the minimum duration of طُهْر?
options: 3 days
10 days
7 days
15 days
questions.explanation: The minimum duration of ṭuhr is 15 days. If spotting occurs before this minimum has elapsed, it is classified as istiḥāḍah, not a new ḥayḍ.

questions.question: حَرَج is a recognized legal basis for concession. Which of the following is another example from fiqh where Sharīʿah removes ḥaraj?
options: The sick person being permitted to pray seated or lying down when unable to stand
Requiring the traveler to combine all five prayers into two
Allowing fasting to be permanently dropped for the elderly
Requiring the sick to pray standing even when in pain
questions.explanation: The sick person is permitted to pray seated or lying down — removing the ḥaraj of an impossible requirement. Similarly, the traveler may shorten four-rakʿah prayers to two.

questions.question: For a ṭalāq to be classified as طَلَاق سُنِّي, how many ṭalāqs may be pronounced at one time?
options: Up to two, as long as there is a gap of one day between them
Only one, pronounced during each separate period of ṭuhr
Up to three, as long as all are pronounced during periods of ṭuhr
Only one, pronounced immediately after each ḥayḍ ends
questions.explanation: For ṭalāq sunnī, the husband pronounces exactly one ṭalāq during each separate period of ṭuhr — never more than one at a time, and never during menstruation.

questions.question: Why is طَوَافُ الزِّيَارَة uniquely critical for a ḥāʾiḍah performing Ḥajj?
options: It is a sunnah that earns great reward but can be compensated by dam
It must be performed while in a state of iḥrām that ṭawāf al-qudūm does not require
It is the only ṭawāf that cannot be delegated to another person
It is a rukn whose omission invalidates the entire Ḥajj and cannot be compensated by dam alone
questions.explanation: Ṭawāf al-ziyārah is a rukn of Ḥajj — its omission invalidates the Ḥajj entirely and cannot be compensated by dam alone; it must ultimately be performed. Ṭawāf al-qudūm is not a rukn and missing it carries no comparable consequence.

questions.question: What is the legal consequence of omitting a رُكْن from an act of worship?
options: The entire act of worship is invalidated and cannot be compensated by dam
The act is valid but requires dam as compensation
The act is valid but must be repeated within the same prayer time
The act is valid but the worshipper must perform an extra rakʿah
questions.explanation: Omitting a rukn invalidates the entire act of worship — it cannot be compensated by dam or any substitute. Omitting a wājib makes the act deficient and requires dam, but the act itself remains valid.
